rows.q: What is BoilerFrame?
rows.answer: **BoilerFrame** is a full-stack web application developed by Rithvik Praveen Kumar that identifies every appearance of a target person in a video. It ingests reference images and footage, then runs a facial-recognition pipeline utilizing AWS Rekognition. The application is built on the **MERN** stack, incorporating technologies like React, Express, MongoDB, and AWS Rekognition. You can find more details in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/rithvikpkx/BoilerFrame).

rows.q: What tech stack does BoilerFrame use?
rows.answer: BoilerFrame uses the MERN stack, which includes **MongoDB**, **Express**, **React**, and **Node.js**. It also integrates **AWS Rekognition** for facial recognition.

rows.q: Tell me about the mind-controlled robotic arm.
rows.answer: The **Mind-Controlled Robotic Arm** is a project by Rithvik Praveen Kumar that demonstrates the feasibility of controlling basic robotic arm movements using thought, acting as a proof-of-concept for a brain-computer interface (BCI). It pairs a NeuroSky EEG headset with an Arduino microprocessor and aims to create a foundation for future BCI work, focusing on translating intent into sign language gestures for differently-abled users. Technologies utilized in this project include `NeuroSky`, `Arduino`, `C++`, and `Python`. You can view a demo of the project [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W8EzUuWgi4o).

rows.q: What headset does the left/right thought prediction project use?

rows.q: How many EEG channels does the thought classifier use?
rows.answer: The thought classifier uses 16-channel EEG data captured with an OpenBCI headset.

rows.q: What is QRIfy and where is it deployed?
rows.answer: QRIfy is a web app that takes user input in the form of text and generates a corresponding downloadable QR code. It was built with a Python and Segno backend, along with a hand-rolled HTML/CSS/JS frontend. QRIfy is deployed on an AWS EC2 instance. You can find its repository on GitHub [here](https://github.com/rithvikpkx/QRCode_Project).

rows.q: What did he build for Habitat for Humanity?

rows.q: What did the citizen happiness project model?
rows.answer: The **Predicting Citizen Happiness** project by Rithvik Praveen Kumar modeled the correlation between national spending in key areas, such as military, education, and health, and reported citizen happiness levels.
